book.title: Creativity: Flow and the Psychology of Discovery and Invention
book.author: Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi

confidence_note: From summaries and the author's lecture, not the book text. The old tree-in-the-forest framing, Bach and Van Gogh, and 'community' as the third part were dropped; the book calls it the field. Einstein example comes from a lecture transcript, not confirmed in the book, so it is flagged low and attributed to a lecture in the story.
facts: Csikszentmihalyi's systems model says creativity arises from three parts: the individual, the domain and the field.
The domain is the body of symbolic rules and procedures, such as mathematics or music.
The field is the group of experts who decide whether a new idea enters the domain, the gatekeepers.
The individual uses the domain's symbols to produce something new.
He defines a creative person as someone whose thoughts or actions change a domain or establish a new one, and a domain cannot be changed without the explicit or implicit consent of the field.
In a lecture he says Einstein's ideas were certified as creative by a small number of leading physics professors.
Where someone lives matters because it decides access to information about the domain, stimulation of novelty and closeness to the field's centres of power (plot summary, medium).
One source illustrates the field with modern art: those who decide which new paintings deserve to be seen, bought and collected, in Manhattan (low; not confirmed as the book's own example).
scene_details: a small number of physics professors certifying Einstein's ideas
tension: A new idea alone is not enough: someone in the field has to accept it.
opening_idea: Open on the Einstein example from the lecture and the small number of professors.

lessons.idea: Find out who judges your work before you polish it
lessons.anchor: the field as gatekeepers; Everyday: someone writing a funding proposal who asks the person who will sign it what they check first

reflect_final: Who in your field would be the first to judge your current work, and what would you ask them to look at?

use_cases.situation: You finished a draft and are about to publish
use_cases.move: Csikszentmihalyi says the field decides what enters the domain. Who is one expert we could ask to look at this first?

use_cases.situation: A friend works alone on a project for years
use_cases.move: Even Einstein's ideas needed physics professors to certify them, per Csikszentmihalyi. Who could look at a part of yours?

use_cases.situation: You doubt whether your work is any good
use_cases.move: I know my domain's rules, but I have never asked the field. I will send one page to one expert.

pocket_idea: Csikszentmihalyi's model has three parts: you, your domain, and the experts who judge. Find your judges early.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: In Csikszentmihalyi's model an idea becomes creative only when the experts of its field accept it.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Csikszentmihalyi says creativity needs three parts: an individual, a domain with its symbolic rules like mathematics or music, and a field of experts who act as gatekeepers. A creative person changes the domain, but only with the field's consent. In a lecture he says a small number of leading physics professors certified Einstein's ideas.
